articles.title: These new Aukey wireless chargers come with cooling fans
articles.summary: Aukey’s new MagFusion chargers offer fast Qi2 wireless charging, with built-in fans that the company says will keep them cool and charging faster than
articles.body: Aukey debuted three new magnetic wireless chargers at IFA in Berlin that come with fans to keep your phone cooler while it’s charging. The company says that means the chargers, called the MagFusion 3-in-1 Pro, the MagFusion GameFrost, and the MagFusion Dash Pro, will charge your phone faster, too. All three use the Qi2 standard, which means up to 15-watt charging for compatible phones and backward compatibility with normal Qi devices. Aukey claims they can drop charging temperatures as much as 68 degrees Fahrenheit compared to “traditional wireless chargers.” The MagFusion 3-in-1 Pro stand can simultaneously charge an iPhone, AirPods, and an Apple Watch. It can tilt up and down over a 30-degree range, also. The MagFusion GameFrost is, as the name implies, meant for gaming sessions, using a thick MagSafe puck-style design (yet with an admirable lack of RGB lights!). Those are both coming later this year for $129.99 and $42.99, respectively. The MagFusion Dash Pro, a vent-mounted charger for your car, is out now and costs $40.99.

articles.title: Apple dials down Liquid Glass, and the Mac looks way better for it
articles.summary: Hands-on with the developer beta of macOS 27 Golden Gate and its reduced Liquid Glass UI. We’re taking an early look at Apple’s upcoming OS for MacBooks and Mac desktops, announced at WWDC.
articles.body: MacOS 27 Golden Gate will usher in a bunch of changes to the Mac when it’s released later this year, with its biggest new features revolving around Siri AI. But for now, using the first developer beta, Siri AI is only offered through a waitlist. So what’s available to try is mostly about how the upcoming operating system looks and feels. Booting up the macOS 27 developer beta upon updating immediately prompts you with Apple’s new Liquid Glass slider, allowing users to set the amount of UI transparency. There’s minimal fanfare to Apple’s welcome screen, but this is reason to celebrate. On one end of the slider, it’s as seethrough as Liquid Glass gets, and on the other end the transparent accents are heavily frosted. Golden Gate starts you in the middle of the slider by default, for just a touch of frosting — perhaps a gentle admission that the original look went too far. You sadly can’t go fully opaque, but this frosted look does greatly reduce the distracting elements of Liquid Glass. [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: After spending just a short while with Golden Gate, I already prefer the minimum transparency look. I’d crank that slider in the full version and never turn back. For the strongest Liquid Glass haters out there, the Reduce Transparency option is still available in the Accessibility settings, but using it is like taking a hammer to all that glass — introducing lots of harsh gray and black backgrounds to the dock, Menu Bar, and Control Center. The absolute wins for macOS 27’s design is the return of edge-to-edge sidebars with colorful icons and the increased corner radii of windows across the OS. The former is basically a backtrack to the way sidebars used to look (which looked better and easier to parse, with less wasted space). And the latter is just logical. How on Earth did Apple get so high on its own design supply that it allowed windowed apps to have mismatched corners? [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: I do have my nitpicks — the new battery icon taken from iOS is less legible (really, I hate it). Also, after Apple finally added the most basic window snapping feature in Sequoia, it hasn’t refined it one bit. Both Tahoe and now Golden Gate are leaving me wanting better and faster tiling controls like Windows 11, as well as the simple ability to rename virtual desktops. But so far, nothing. Apple says Golden Gate is supposed to feel snappier, with faster search indexing. It’s too early to tell how much of a difference this makes on the MacBook Neo I’m testing it on — especially since dev betas are notoriously buggy and unstable. Using Spotlight search for local files on Golden Gate performed similar to another Neo I had on-hand running macOS 26 Tahoe. And opening apps on both systems side by side led to mixed results: Golden Gate opened Lightroom Classic and Slack faster, but Tahoe was faster to open Photoshop and Steam. I hope Apple’s under the hood improvements to memory and CPU usage will really show on the MacBook Neo, which could use all the efficiency it can get, but the jury’s out for now. [Image: [Image: The new battery icon (left) is worse than the old one (right). I don’t care if it’s more cohesive with iOS — it’s harder to read than the old percentage. There’s still more to come with further beta releases of macOS 27, where we’ll at some point be able to fully test Siri AI, Visual Intelligence, and the revamped Spotlight Search. Last year’s power user-focused Spotlight with clipboard history was a nice improvement, but I’m skeptical that Siri AI being baked into Spotlight will be quite the game changer Apple’s billing it as. I’ll keep an open mind and be looking to find out once I’m off the waitlist. For now, I’m relieved Apple is slightly backpedaling on Liquid Glass. While the look was never quite as bad on the Mac as it was on iOS, it’s a welcome change to be able to turn down these transparencies and get a little closer to the old looks from Sequoia. That and the other bits of UI polish are a nice upgrade on their own. Now, Apple has to show that it can nail all the new AI features, too — I’m eager to see how it fares. Update, June 9th: Updated article to reflect that the developer beta for macOS 27 Golden Gate now immediately presents you with the Liquid Glass slider at the welcome screen. This did not initially happen with the first Mac we updated. Also added a screenshot of this to the first image gallery.

articles.title: My first 24 hours with Siri AI on the Mac
articles.summary: We tested Apple’s new Siri AI assistant on the Mac, currently in an early preview on macOS 27 Golden Gate developer beta.
articles.body: I turned off Siri on the Mac years ago and never looked back. Similarly, I found Apple Intelligence so fruitless I never engage with it. But the new Siri AI coming to macOS 27 Golden Gate has at least got me slightly rethinking things. I’m still early in testing Siri AI, as I’ve only had access to it in the macOS 27 developer beta for little more than 24 hours. It’s also in an early preview state on the dev beta, so there should be lots of runway for improvements before it releases later this year. I don’t even know if it’s done indexing my files and folders on our review unit M5 MacBook Air and M5 Max MacBook Pro. Unlike on the iOS 27 dev beta, there’s no “indexing in progress” box in the settings page. I asked Siri if it could tell me, but it told me to click a button in Settings that isn’t there. My colleagues got a headstart testing Siri AI on the iPhone and Apple Watch, and getting a read on its general vibe, and they’ve so far had some positive feedback from using it. My feelings are a little more mixed. [Image: A frequent reminder that Siri AI is in early preview on a macOS developer beta. I get a fair amount of these. When I sit down at a laptop I don’t need a voice assistant for searching things I’m randomly curious about or checking the weather like I would on a phone; I can do that faster and more accurately with keyboard and mouse. So I tried to think of ways to let Siri AI help me on macOS — things that might actually be useful to me in my everyday work. I’d be happy to automate some of the time-consuming benchmarking I do when reviewing laptops, but although Siri AI can launch apps, it can’t take actions inside them (not that Apple ever claimed it could). I then tried to see if vibe coding a couple Shortcuts could get me there instead. This isn’t a Siri AI feature, but it is a new part of Apple Intelligence. I asked Shortcuts to run a test in either Geekbench or Cinebench, capture the results in a screenshot, wait a few minutes, and repeat the process two more times. But the resulting automations couldn’t actually run the tests either. Apple Intelligence made a shortcut that opened Geekbench and took screenshots (but forgot about actually running the benchmark), and it made a Cinebench shortcut that had “Wait for you to run the test” as an actual step. Maybe if developers continue expanding App Intents this could one day work. [Image: [Image: So if Siri can’t help me run my benchmarks, maybe it can at least help me be a little faster in logging the data. In my normal workflow, I run each benchmark three times, taking screenshots as I go, and later average out the results before cataloging them in a spreadsheet. Apple’s WWDC keynote showed someone using Ask Siri in Spotlight to analyze data in local files. So I tried selecting batches of those screenshots in Finder and asking Siri to calculate the average scores for me. It worked pretty well — most of the time. It was smart enough to distinguish single-core CPU scores from multicore CPU scores and GPU scores, average the test results, and arrange them in easy-to-read tables. But it could get thrown off if I included screenshots of too many different types of tests, especially if I mixed ones with synthetic score results (Geekbench, PugetBench, etc.) and time-based results (Blender render tests and our 4K video export test). And it sometimes got thrown off by the CPU rankings data that’s visible in Cinebench screenshots. Ideally, I’d be able to have Siri AI accurately calculate the 15 or so averages from my dozens of screenshots all at once — that would save me some serious time. But for now, it can at best only help me a little bit. And unless it gets better I’m still inclined to continue doing it all myself, especially since Siri messed up the numbers a couple times by pulling the wrong data. [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: So far, Siri AI seems a lot more capable within Apple’s ecosystem than it is outside of it, even for apps and files that are already on my Mac but in non-Apple apps. When I asked Siri to find my pictures of cats or babies, it pulled up results from Apple’s Photos and Messages apps. This could be enough for plenty of people, but not for me. Most of my messaging is done in Signal, and photos from my phone are uploaded to Google Photos, not iCloud. Siri also missed the thousands of images I have in my Lightroom Classic catalog, even though the files are stored locally in the Pictures folder and I kept asking it to access them directly. It’s possible those files haven’t been indexed yet, but I have no way to tell. For now, I’m getting similar vibes to when I tested Copilot Vision last year. Like Copilot Vision, you can use Siri’s Visual Intelligence to ask questions about things on your screen. And like Copilot, it’s limited. I asked Siri to evaluate benchmark results on a spreadsheet in Google Sheets, but it can’t see all the data if it’s not visible onscreen all at once. I could get it to see the whole spreadsheet by downloading it as an Excel file and pointing Siri at it in Finder, but when I asked for the laptop with the highest single-core Geekbench score it gave me multicore data. Not great. [Image: No, Siri, those are not single core scores. And those columns could not be more clearly labeled. I opened Siri while running Lightroom Classic, on a black-and-white photo from my Ricoh GR IV Monochrome review, and asked Siri how to make it look more like a shot from street photographer Alan Schaller. Siri offered specific value adjustments for exposure, contrast, and so on, and adjusting those values gave me a decent result. Unfortunately, when I asked Siri to judge the result, it went sycophant on me, saying I’d nailed the look and achieved an “almost timeless feel,” which is the type of behavior Apple says it’s not supposed to show. (I thought we were past this.) Then I uploaded a classic Garry Winograd photo and asked how to change my Lightroom settings to match that photo; Siri recommended I set the exposure to the value it was already at. So, some hits and some misses. [Image: This was an image that just barely made the cut in my Ricoh GR IV Monochrome review, but I guess Siri isn’t going to tell me that my photos are mid at best. It’s still very early days for Siri AI, and much can change between now and the final release. But what’s clear already is that the experience is likely to be very different on an iPhone, where so much of your data is held inside Apple’s apps, and on a Mac, where you’re likely to be bouncing between all kinds of apps and ecosystems in ways that limit what Siri can do. Even so, it’s faint praise, but this is still the most useful and helpful Siri has been. It’s baby’s first real AI steps for Apple.

articles.body: Apple has introduced its first-ever foldable iPhone, the iPhone Duo, alongside the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max. The foldable iPhone Duo features a 7.6-inch inner display and a 5.4-inch outer display, while the iPhone 18 Pro models bring a new 48MP Fusion Main camera with variable aperture and longer battery life. All three models run on the A20 Pro chip, while the iPhone Duo is eSIM-only.Apple has also announced India pricing, storage variants and availability for the new models. Here’s a detailed look at the prices, availability and key features of the newly launched iPhone Duo, iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max models.​Apple iPhone Duo, iPhone 18 Pro and Phone 18 Pro Max India price and availabilityThe iPhone Duo comes in Star White and Night Sky colours. It is available in four storage options.StorageIndia Price256GBRs 2,99,900512GBRs 3,24,9001TBRs 3,74,9002TBRs 4,49,900Pre-orders for iPhone Duo begin October 16, with availability starting October 23 in India and more than 70 countries and regions. The phone will become available in another 28 countries and regions from October 30. iPhone Duo comes with an eSIM-only design worldwide. Apple says more than 500 carriers support eSIM, including Airtel, Jio and Vi.​The iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max come in black, silver, glacier and burgundy finishes. Both models are available in four storage options.Apple iPhone 18 Pro: India price and availabilityStorageIndia Price256GBRs 1,64,900512GBRs 1,89,9001TBRs 2,39,9002TBRs 3,14,900Apple iPhone 18 Pro Max: India price and availabilityStorageIndia Price256GBRs 1,79,900512GBRs 2,04,9001TBRs 2,54,9002TBRs 3,29,900Pre-orders for iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max begin September 12, with availability starting September 18 in India and more than 65 countries and regions. The two models will become available in another 20 countries and regions from September 25.Both models come with iOS 27 and support Apple Intelligence and Siri AI. eSIM-only models are available in select markets, while India is among the countries included in the initial launch.​Apple iPhone Duo: Key highlightsApple's iPhone Duo, the company's first foldable iPhone, opens to a 7.6-inch display, which is the largest ever on an iPhone. It folds down to a 5.4-inch outer Super Retina XDR screen that Apple says offers 90 per cent of the screen area of the iPhone 18 Pro. Both displays share the same aspect ratio for proportional scaling, support ProMotion, Always-On functionality and up to 3,000 nits of peak brightness, and the inner display uses a nano-texture, glare-reducing finish with an under-display FaceTime camera.​Design: The device is built from grade 5 titanium with a mirror-polished finish, Ceramic Shield on the back and the tougher Ceramic Shield 2 on the front, and carries an IP68 water/dust resistance rating. Its hinge has over 100 components, reinforced with support ribs and ceramic fibre inserts for added rigidity.​Cameras: iPhone Duo has a 48MP Fusion Main camera, a 48MP Fusion Ultra Wide (shared with the iPhone 18 Pro), and a Center Stage front camera. Fold-specific features include Smart Take, Duo Preview, Kid Cue and Duo FaceTime, plus 4K/120fps Dolby Vision video recording.​Software: It ships with iOS 27, redesigned for the foldable form factor with side-mounted controls, dual Home Screen pages, Split View multitasking, an upgraded StandBy mode, and a beta rollout of Siri AI, which can use personal context and on-screen content to answer questions or take actions.​Performance and battery: The phone runs on Apple’s 2nm A20 Pro chip (6-core CPU, 7-core GPU, dual 16-core Neural Engine) with a vapour chamber cooling system. Dual batteries can last up to 31 hours of video on the inner display, 44 hours on the outer display or 24 hours of mixed use, and it has fast wired and wireless charging.​Connectivity: It uses Apple's N1 chip (Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, Thread) and the C2 modem for improved cellular performance, with Apple Pencil (USB-C) support planned later this year.​Apple iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max: Key highlightsDisplay: Both models feature Super Retina XDR displays with ProMotion, Always-On functionality and up to 3,000 nits of peak outdoor brightness. The Dynamic Island has been redesigned to take up less space while showing more information, including up to three Live Activities at once.Cameras: The iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max feature a new 48MP Fusion Main camera with variable aperture, bringing manual aperture control to the iPhone for the first time. The six-blade system offers four aperture settings and can automatically adjust based on lighting and depth of field. These phones also get upgraded Photographic Styles, Pro controls for settings such as shutter speed and white balance, and a histogram for checking exposure. Apple Reference Image can create a reference version of a photo using signed sensor data to help determine whether an image has been edited. Video features include Cinematic effects after capture at up to 60fps, 4K Dolby Vision HDR time-lapse and an updated Audio Mix.Performance: Both models are powered by Apple's 2nm A20 Pro chip with a 6-core CPU, 7-core GPU and Dual 16-core Neural Engine. Apple says the GPU is up to 40 per cent faster than the A19 Pro, while the Neural Engine delivers twice the AI processing power. The phones also use a redesigned vapour chamber with three times more surface area than the previous generation, enabling up to 40 per cent higher sustained performance, according to Apple.Battery: The iPhone 18 Pro offers up to 36 hours of video playback on eSIM-only models, while the iPhone 18 Pro Max offers up to 45 hours. The iPhone 18 Pro can charge up to 50 per cent in around 15 minutes and wirelessly charge up to 50 per cent in 30 minutes. Apple says five minutes of wired charging on the iPhone 18 Pro Max provides around seven hours of video playback, while the phone can offer up to 30 hours of usage on a full charge based on its new battery usage model.Software: Both phones ship with iOS 27 and support Apple Intelligence and Siri AI. Siri AI can use personal context from messages, emails and photos, understand onscreen content and help users find information or perform actions. iOS 27 also introduces iPhone Handoff, allowing users with supported carriers to switch between two iPhone models using the same phone number.Connectivity: The iPhone 18 Pro models feature Apple's N1 wireless chip with Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6 and Thread support. They also introduce the C2 cellular modem system, which Apple says provides faster uploads than C1X while consuming 15 per cent less energy.​Get the latest technology news and updates. articles.title: 10 biggest features of Apple's first foldable phone, iPhone Duo
articles.summary: Tech News News: Apple has launched iPhone Duo, its first foldable iPhone, bringing a new design to the iPhone lineup. The iPhone Duo opens to reveal a 7.6-inch inner .
articles.body: Apple has launched iPhone Duo, its first foldable iPhone, bringing a new design to the iPhone lineup. The iPhone Duo opens to reveal a 7.6-inch inner display and folds down to a 5.4-inch outer display for regular use. Apple says iPhone Duo is built with a titanium frame, a new hinge, dual batteries and the A20 Pro chip. The new smartphone also brings changes to the camera, iOS 27, multitasking and Apple Intelligence. Price of Apple iPhone Duo starts at Rs 2,99,900 for the 256GB model with pre-orders beginning on October 16. Apple iPhone Duo will go on sale starting October 23. In this article, we look at the 10 biggest iPhone Duo features announced by Apple.1. Apple iPhone Duo display: 7.6-inch foldable screenThe biggest change is the foldable screen. When opened, the iPhone Duo has a 7.6-inch Super Retina XDR display. Apple says the inner screen is 50 percent larger than the display on the iPhone 18 Pro Max. It has a nano-texture finish designed to reduce glare and reflections. The inner display also supports ProMotion, Always On and up to 3,000 nits of peak outdoor brightness.When folded, users get a 5.4-inch Super Retina XDR outer display. Apple says it provides 90 percent of the screen area of the iPhone 18 Pro.2. Apple iPhone Duo design: Titanium body and new hingeApple has used grade 5 titanium for the iPhone Duo enclosure. The phone also has a new hinge made from more than 100 components. The company says the hinge controls the opening and closing of the phone and supports the centre of the folding display.The inner screen uses a scratch-resistant coating, a nano-textured cover layer and high-strength glass. Apple has also used custom adhesives and a titanium plate below the folding display. Apple iPhone Duo has an IP68 rating, and is splash, water and dust resistant.3. Apple iPhone Duo processor: A20 Pro chip and performanceThe iPhone Duo is powered by Apple's A20 Pro chip, the same chip used in the iPhone 18 Pro models. Apple says the chip is built using 2nm process technology and has a six-core CPU and seven-core GPU. According to Apple, the CPU is up to 20 percent faster than the A19 Pro, while the GPU is up to 40 percent faster and more power efficient.The chip also has a Dual 16-core Neural Engine, which Apple says provides twice the compute power for on-device AI models.4. Apple iPhone Duo battery: Dual-battery setup and chargingThe foldable iPhone uses one battery on each side of the device. Apple says its silicon and energy-management system allow the two batteries to work together as one. The company claims up to 31 hours of video playback when using the inner display and up to 44 hours when using the outer display.When both displays are used equally, Apple says the phone can provide up to 24 hours of usage per charge. The phone can charge up to 50 percent in about 20 minutes. Wireless charging can reach 50 percent in around 30 minutes using a MagSafe or Qi2 charger.5. Apple iPhone Duo camera: 48MP Fusion camerasThe iPhone Duo comes with a 48MP Fusion Main camera. Apple says it can capture photos at up to 48MP and has an integrated optical-quality 2x Telephoto option. The main camera also has sensor-shift optical image stabilisation, a large sensor and a fast aperture for low-light photography.The phone also has a 48MP Fusion Ultra Wide camera that supports macro photography.6. Apple iPhone Duo camera features: Smart Take, Duo Preview and moreApple has added camera features that use the two displays. Smart Take uses on-device AI models to analyse a scene and automatically capture a photo when people are ready. With Duo Preview, people being photographed can see the live camera preview on the outer display. This can help them check their framing and pose.The phone also allows users to take selfies using the higher-resolution rear cameras while viewing the shot on the outer screen. Another feature called Duo FaceTime allows people around the phone to join a video call using the outer display. For children, Kid Cue can show Peanuts animations on the outer screen to get their attention while taking a photo.7. Apple iPhone Duo video: 4K 120fps Dolby Vision recordingThe iPhone Duo supports 4K video recording at 120fps in Dolby Vision using its 48MP Fusion Main camera. Apple says users can use this for slow-motion video. The phone also supports Cinematic effects after recording at up to 60fps. Its Audio Mix feature uses new algorithms to improve voices and separate music. Additinlly, time-lapse recording is also supported in 4K Dolby Vision HDR.8. Apple iPhone Duo software: iOS 27 and split-screen multitaskingApple has changed iOS 27 for the foldable display. When the phone is open, users can access two Home Screen pages and Today View. The system also moves some controls to the side to make more room for content. The iPhone Duo also supports Split View, allowing two apps to run side by side for the first time on an iPhone.Users can also open two windows from the same app, such as Safari, and save pairs of apps for later use. Apple says apps including Netflix, Zoom and Slack have already been adapted for the foldable design.9. Apple iPhone Duo AI features: Apple Intelligence and Siri AIThe iPhone Duo supports Apple Intelligence and the new Siri AI. Siri AI is rolling out in beta with iOS 27. articles.title: The Trump phone just got a $250 price hike
articles.summary: Even the Trumps can’t escape RAMageddon.﻿
articles.body: Bad news if you didn’t lock in a Trump phone at launch: It now costs $749, a $250 increase on its price at launch. The T1 Phone itself hasn’t changed. Trump Mobile didn’t announce the price increase, instead quietly changing its website overnight. This wasn’t a total surprise though, especially given the phone ships with an unexpectedly generous 512GB of storage and 12GB of RAM. When I spoke to two Trump Mobile executives earlier this year, they called the $499 launch pricing “introductory,” and a few months later, the website itself was changed to reflect that, calling it a “promotional price.” That wording is now gone. When I reviewed the Trump phone in July, I wasn’t especially impressed, even at $499. At $749 there is absolutely no reason recommend it. You could buy an iPhone 17E or Galaxy S26 FE and have $50 left over to buy a gold case; $50 more would net you an older flagship like the iPhone 16 or Pixel 10. Any one of these phones would blow the T1 Phone out of the water. To my surprise, my Trump phone has received some support since it launched. There’s been exactly one software update, moving it from Android’s February 2026 security patch to the May 2026 version. It’s still running Android 15 though, which is now two years old. While the Trump phone officially started shipping in May, almost a year after it was announced, it remains unclear just how many customers have received their phones. A report from the BBC last month found that at least some buyers still say their phones never arrived.

articles.title: The variable aperture isn’t the cool part of the iPhone 18 Pro’s camera
articles.summary: Apple announced the iPhone 18 Pro and and Pro Max alongside its new iPhone Duo foldable phone. The new camera feature of the Pro phones is a variable aperture. But will it make a big difference?
articles.body: Apple always makes a big show of the latest cameras in its phones, and the major talking point of the iPhone 18 Pro is about the new variable aperture. Both the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max have an adjustable mechanical iris in their main camera modules to let more or less light into the sensor, allowing users to shoot at f/1.48, f/1.8, f/2.8, and f/4. You can, of course, let the camera select your aperture automatically, but the manual aperture control comes along with other new pro controls allowing you to dial in shutter speeds, manual white balance, and even manual focusing. As a whole, this is a wealth of new controls for an iPhone camera. You’d normally have to install a third-party camera app like Halide to do some of this, and now it’s all just baked into the 18 Pro’s native camera app. (It’s almost as if Apple poached a key person directly from Halide.) But I’d temper any expectations over the variable aperture being the standout feature. It’s going to be mid, at best. [Image: [Image: [Image: Why? Because smartphone sensors are still pretty dang tiny, and most subjects are in reasonable focus until you get really close. And stopping down to f/4 is unlikely to blow you away with much sharper results like it does in full-size cameras or any special qualities aside from some sunstar effects in very particular lighting scenarios. In fact, due to lens diffraction, your photos might be less sharp at f/4 than f/1.8 or f/2.8. What you’re most likely to benefit from by stopping down the lens is more depth of field with close-up subjects, getting more people in focus during big group shots with plenty of light (where people aren’t all lined up together), and more flexibility in shooting video in overly bright situations (like direct sunlight). That might prove useful for those particular situations, but they’re likely to be few and far between. And smartphone sensors are small enough to already have plenty in focus at midrange and further distances, even when shot wide open. It’s probably why other brands like Samsung and Xiaomi have experimented with variable apertures but quietly ditched them. I think the real star feature of the iPhone 18 Pro’s camera is its f/1.48 maximum aperture. Fuck stopping down, man. People love bokeh. [Image: [Image: Last year’s Pro iPhone cameras had an f/1.7 aperture, and now being at f/1.48, the 18 Pro camera should work better in low-light as well as have a slightly shallower depth of field. Will f/1.48 be a huge difference in bokeh from f/1.7? Probably not. It’s likely to have depth of field that’s just a smidge shallower — but that’s the look that people often like. I speak from experience here, as I usually shoot on full-frame cameras and one of my go-to lenses is a 50mm with an f/1.2 maximum aperture. A lens that fast, with depth of field that shallow gives a unique look that’s easy to overuse, but it almost never fails that people swoon when I take their portrait using that lens — with that blurry, “dreamy” blur isolating them from the background. The f/1.48 of the iPhone 18 Pro is obviously not going to compare to an f/1.2 on full-frame, but f/1.2 and similarly wide apertures on big sensors is the look that people often want to emulate. It’s the whole reason Portrait Modes on smartphones came into being in the first place. The iPhone 18 Pro is likely to have a very good camera just like most top-flight smartphones have very good cameras. The added controls are exciting and fun, even if I don’t always want to be bothered with manual controls when taking quick snapshots. It’ll be nice to have them right at your fingertips without having to install a more specialized app. Just don’t be surprised if you start ignoring that aperture setting after some initial tinkering in the new phone honeymoon phase. But even long after that, f/1.48 will be the gift that should keep on giving.

articles.title: From school expulsion to free gurukul: A UP man’s journey of change on KBC
articles.summary: Uddeshya Sachan's journey from being expelled from school to establishing a free learning space for 400 underprivileged children highlights resilience and the spirit of social change, featured on KBC 18.
articles.body: Uddeshya Sachan, a KBC 18 contestant from Uttar Pradesh, shares on the show how childhood experiences of financial crisis and school expulsion shaped his decision to build a learning space that now educates around 400 students without charging fees. Recounting the severe financial crisis his family faced, which required him to work multiple jobs to fund his own education, Uddeshya opens up about the pivotal moment that changed his life's purpose by saying, "Sir, mere pitaji tailor the aur mummy ko ek baar current lag gaya tha toh bimaar thi. Ghar ki sthiti bahut kharab thi, rishtedaar thodi madad kar rahe the. Humare paas school ki fees dene ke liye paise nahi the, toh mujhe aur mere bhai ko nikal diya. Pitaji ki sthiti aisi nahi thi lekin unhone bahut sangharsh kiya, chaar hazaar ya paanch hazaar mein ghar chal raha tha. Dheere dheere kaise toh padhai poori hui. Ek moment mein aisa feel hua ki main akela nahi hoon, mere jaise aur bhi bachche honge. Maine joh mehsoos kiya, aur bhi bachchon ne mehsoos kiya hoga. Phir socha, maine idhar janam liya hai, toh jab main marunga mujhe kuch achha karke marna hain aur society mein kuch change lana hain."Deeply moved by Uddeshya’s grit, host Amitabh Bachchan praises his noble initiative and the immense satisfaction that comes from achieving such a meaningful goal by saying, "Uddeshyaji, main samajhta hoon aapne kaafi sangharsh kiya, lekin sangharsh karke jab aap jeevan mein uthte hain, aap bohot kuch seekhte hain. Ek aapka uddeshya hai ki humein jivan mein kahi toh pahunchna hain, aur usse poora karne ke baad joh santusti milti hain, uske liye aapko bahut bahut badhai."When asked how he manages the resources for 400 students, Uddeshya reveals that his mother initially supported him financially, and he slowly began sharing videos of his school on social media one of which was even amplified by actor R Madhavan. Hearing this, Mr. Amitabh Bachchan makes a heartwarming promise on national television to personally support Uddeshya's cause by saying, "Uddeshyaji, aapka joh social media hain aur usko joh sambhalte hain, unko bolna humein bhi bhejna. Aur humare paas bhi ek kuch log hain joh social media pe aate hain, toh unko hum bhej denge aur phir aapko patra likhenge ki humne aapka kaam kar diya hain."Get the latest TV News, TV Shows and more. articles.title: iPhone 18 Pro launch: Here's why Apple did not launch successor of the ‘world's most-popular’ iPhone
articles.summary: Tech News News: Apple has launched the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max and iPhone Duo – its first foldable smartphone – at its Surprise and Shine event. Fans also ex.
articles.body: Apple has launched the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max and iPhone Duo – its first foldable smartphone – at its Surprise and Shine event. Fans also expected the Cupertino-based company to also unveil iPhone 18, the successor of the iPhone 17 that emerged as the world's bestselling smartphone in 2026 in the second quarter of 2026 (Q2 2026). Instead, the company broke from years of tradition. Rather than unveiling an entry-level iPhone 18 alongside its high-end tier, Apple reserved the keynote exclusively for premium hardware.The regular iPhone 18 was entirely missing from the presentation. However, reports claim that the baseline variant has not been scrapped – it has simply been pushed back to early 2027 as part of a deliberate operational pivot.Why Apple moved away from its all-at-once September playbookHistorically, Apple introduced its base and Pro models side by side each September, and rode a massive holiday revenue wave across North America and Europe. The decision to separate the portfolio into two distinct launch cycles may be a signal to several strategic considerations.First, it is likely that management may have opted to avoid saturating a single autumn window with too many competing models as the company launched a folding iPhone Duo.Secondly, memory shortages across global tech supply chains may have presented major manufacturing hurdles, making it difficult to satisfy massive launch-day demand across both budget-friendly and ultra-premium lines simultaneously. According to news agency Reuters, holding back more affordable variants until the spring allows Apple to spread device shipments more evenly across four financial quarters rather than relying disproportionately on the end-of-year rush.What lies ahead for the Spring 2027 rosterIt is to be noted that Apple has not confirmed the timeline of iPhone 18 launch, but by dedicating the September stage to its high-margin Pro devices and the foldable Duo, Apple may have cleared the runway for a second high-profile consumer hardware wave in the early months of 2027.The upcoming spring release cycle is expected to feature three distinct devices aimed at a broader consumer base. As per MacRumors, the baseline model will adopt the 2nm A20 silicon, increased RAM, a reduced Dynamic Island footprint, and Apple’s in-house C2 cellular modem, using cost-effective display glass and shared parts to manage consumer costs.iPhone 18e: Positioned as the follow-up to the iPhone 17e, this tier is slated to carry an upgraded processor and 9GB of unified system memory.iPhone Air 2: Reports indicate an updated ultra-thin build may introduce an added secondary camera sensor alongside an expanded internal battery.iPhone 17 was the best-selling phone in Q2 2026Recently, a report by Counterpoint Research said that the standard iPhone 17 captured 6% of global smartphone sales in the April-June quarter, becoming the most popular smartphone in Q2 2026. The iPhone 17 Pro Max and iPhone 17 Pro, on the other hand, took the next two spots. The research firm said the base iPhone 17 benefited from upgrades that helped narrow the gap between the standard and Pro models.Get the latest technology news and updates. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: Why iPhones are so expensive in India, again
articles.summary: Tech News News: The best time to buy a new iPhone was yesterday. That's been the going wisdom for years, and today it's just a statement of fact. Apple's first foldab.
articles.body: The best time to buy a new iPhone was yesterday. That's been the going wisdom for years, and today it's just a statement of fact. Apple's first foldable, the iPhone Duo, lands in India at Rs 2,99,900. The iPhone 18 Pro starts at Rs 1,64,900. Can’t exactly say nobody was surprised. But new phones get new prices, and we'd been told for months that this year's would sting.The older iPhones getting pricier wasn't a surprise, even though it broke from how this usually works. Prices don't normally move once a phone's already on shelves for a year, it rather go down. But Tim Cook had already said as much. Nobody was caught off guard when it landed. The iPhone 17 launched last year at Rs 82,900 and it's Rs 99,900 now. The 17e went up from Rs 64,900 to Rs 79,900. The Air was Rs 1,19,900 and it's Rs 1,49,900. Nothing about either phone changed overnight except the price.What nobody had priced in was how much of that increase would land here. Older iPhones in the US went up by a flat $100. The same phones in India went up by two and three times that.Some of it is cost. Some of it is a decision. Telling the two apart is worth doing here, because the difference matters more here than it would anywhere else.India was an expensive place to buy an iPhone, until it wasn'tIndia didn't get the first iPhone at all. The 2007 model never launched here. What we got, in 2008, was the iPhone 3G at Rs 31,000, about three times what an American was paying for the same handset.Ten years on, not much had changed. The iPhone X came in at Rs 89,000 in 2017 while the US paid $999, which worked out to something near Rs 64,000 at the time. A quarter of the Indian price was tax, duty and the cost of getting the box into the country. Duty went up twice in those years. If you wanted an iPhone you got it at duty free, or you asked a cousin flying back from Dubai, or you didn't get one.Then Apple started building them here and the maths changed. First the SE, then the vanilla models, until Pros were rolling out within weeks of a Cupertino launch. The base price stopped climbing. The iPhone 12 launched at Rs 79,900 in 2020, and so did the 13, the 14, the 15 and the 16. The Pros were being priced with some restraint too. The 16 Pro actually launched below the 15 Pro, at Rs 1,19,900. The 16e came in under all of them at Rs 59,900. The stores opened in Mumbai and Delhi. No cost EMI turned Rs 79,900 into a monthly number many never thought twice about.Five years of that, and the iPhone stopped being something many saved up for. It worked, too. India moved into Apple's top handful of markets by shipments, the sort of place the company started naming on earnings calls instead of grouping into "rest of world".Apple's position here is secure enough. What moved this week were the prices underneath it. The cheapest new iPhone you can buy today is Rs 20,000 above where the entry model sat eighteen months ago, and the 17e alone is up Rs 15,000 since March. It isn't even six months old yet.A good part of this has nothing to do with AppleA fair bit of the gap is just tax and duty. Tarun Pathak, research director at Counterpoint Research, breaks the Duo's India price into a stack. Around 17 percent import duty. Another 18 percent GST. By his estimate, a further 5 to 6 percent from currency movement. That's past 40 percent before Apple has decided anything about margin, and the Duo takes the full hit, because it won't be assembled here for a while and lands as a finished import.That's how a $1,999 phone reaches you at Rs 2,99,900, and Rs 4,49,900 if you want the 2TB one. It's also why the iPhones made here sit much closer to their dollar price. The 17 Pro was $1,099 in the US and Rs 1,34,900 here. The 18 Pro is $1,199 and Rs 1,64,900. Those are gaps you can at least follow. The Duo's is nothing like it.That stack also explains why a dollar increase never arrives here as a dollar increase. Duty and GST are percentages, so they scale with whatever Apple adds at the top. A $100 rise is roughly Rs 8,800 to begin with, and by the time GST has been applied, and duty too if the phone is imported, it reaches a shelf here at somewhere between Rs 10,000 and Rs 12,000. Every cost increase Apple absorbs globally gets amplified on the way into this market, and this year there were a lot of them.None of that is new, though. The same stack was in place last year, and last year it still put the iPhone 17 on shelves at Rs 82,900.Taxes explains the level, what it doesn't explain is the jump.What moved is the memory, and Apple did warn us. Back in June, Tim Cook sat down for an interview with one purpose: to say that price rises were coming and couldn't be avoided. He wouldn't say which products or by how much. He called what's happening to memory a hundred-year flood, and said that in forty years around the electronics supply chain he'd never seen anything like it. People took the hint. The advice going around ever since has been to buy whatever Apple product you were planning to buy, immediately.He was talking about memory, which covers two things on a spec sheet. The RAM a phone runs on and the storage it fills up. Both used to get cheaper every cycle, reliably, for four decades. That's stopped. Supply chain estimates put 16GB of smartphone DRAM at roughly $42 in mid 2025 and roughly $181 a year later. Those are dollar figures, and they stay dollar figures no matter where the phone is eventually put together.The reason is AI, which by now you could have guessed.The three companies that make almost all the world's memory also make the high-bandwidth memory that AI servers run on, and that business pays better, ships in bigger volumes and comes with multiyear contracts. Apple used to have enough leverage to squeeze those suppliers down to almost nothing. Now it waits in line like everybody else. Ternus spent yesterday's keynote arguing that the iPhone is already the best AI device anybody has built, and the same AI is why it costs what it does.Everyone is passing it on. The Pixel 11 came in at $899 against $799 for the Pixel 10, and at Rs 89,999 here, with every model in the family costing more than the Pixel 10 it replaced. Samsung's Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra sits at about Rs 2 lakh and the Fold 8 at Rs 1,79,999, the most Samsung has ever charged for a foldable in India. Anything with a chip in it has been getting dearer all year: laptops, consoles, cars, the lot. Apple was late to it the way it was late to foldables, and it won't be early to the recovery either. Memory fabs take years to build, and most forecasts don't have supply catching demand before late 2027.The rest of it is a decision Apple madeRun that multiplier on the iPhone 17 and you get to about Rs 12,000. The price went up by Rs 17,000. On the Air it went up by Rs 30,000. Tax and duty do not get you there.There's a pattern in how the increases were applied, too. In the US every older model went up by the same $100, which works out to 10 percent on the Air and closer to 17 percent on the 17e. Here the increases were far more even in percentage terms, roughly 20 to 25 percent on each of the 17, the 17e and the Air, whatever the phone cost to begin with. A component shock lands as a fixed cost per device. What was applied here looks more like the whole ladder being reset.The Air is where that shows up worst. It was always a slightly strange buy, a thin phone with one camera at Rs 1,19,900, sold on how it felt rather than what it did. At Rs 1,49,900 it now sits Rs 15,000 under a current generation iPhone 18 Pro. In the US the same two phones are $100 apart on a much bigger base. The middle of the range here hasn't just moved up, it has been squeezed flat.Prabhu Ram, who heads the industry research group at CyberMedia Research, puts the rest down to a list of things that have nothing to do with components: the rupee, local tax structure, channel economics, and Apple's own reading of what India's affluent buyers are willing to spend. The channel part matters more here than most people assume. Apple sells the bulk of its phones in the US directly. Here it moves through distributors, large format retail and thousands of smaller stores, and every one of those margins sits inside the price on the sticker.Then there's the last variable, which is Apple's judgement. It has never converted its American price and printed the sticker. It prices each market on what it thinks that market will pay, and it has seemingly decided we'll pay quite a lot.None of this works without the financing, though. The Duo comes to about Rs 48,800 a month across six no-cost instalments and the 18 Pro to about Rs 26,300, and the monthly figure is what the people buying these phones actually respond to. It also means the Rs 30,000 that went onto the Air reaches a buyer as Rs 5,000 a month, which is far easier to absorb than it looks on a price list.The aspirational class explanation is one you'll have heard for a decade now, and it keeps being the right one. India's aspirational class, the way Ram reads it, is still confident about discretionary spending, particularly on things that work as premium lifestyle statements. That gives Apple room at the top of the range it doesn't have in most markets.The lineup shows it better than any single price does. The Duo isn't here to sell in volume. It sits above the Pro Max as a new ultra premium tier, a halo that lifts the average selling price of everything below it, and Pathak expects it to grow India's foldable segment by value long before it does by volume. The Pro line has taken a 20 to 22 percent increase, and that's where the memory cost is actually being passed on.Then there's what Apple hasn't done. There's no standard iPhone 18 this year. That phone, the 18e and a second Air are all expected around March. The base iPhone 17 went up instead of coming down the way last year's model always does. So the usual move, buying the previous phone at a discount, isn't on the table until spring. Anyone who would have made that move and still wants a current iPhone gets pointed at the Pro, and the Pro is what lifts the average.None of which means Apple sells less here in rupee terms. Pathak expects volumes to slip while revenue keeps climbing, a low single digit decline in units against 6 to 7 percent growth in value. The mix does it. Apple grew 2 percent year on year between January and July, the Pro series grew 32 percent over the same stretch, and Pro's share of Apple's India sales is on track to go from 11 percent last year to about 15 percent by the end of this one.A lot rides on the festive quarter now, on trade-in schemes and on older iPhones continuing to sell, the iPhone 15 included. Pathak also sees the refurbished market growing faster than anyone had planned for, and that's hard to argue with. Every buyer pushed up the ladder leaves a phone behind.That is also the quiet reason increases keep getting absorbed here. An iPhone holds its value better than anything else sold in this market, so what a buyer actually pays over two or three years has never risen as fast as the sticker suggests. A Rs 99,900 phone that fetches half of that on trade-in is a different proposition from a Rs 99,900 phone that fetches a quarter.There's even a case that Apple comes out of this ahead of its rivals, because budget and mid-range Android makers have nowhere near the margin to absorb a shock like this one. Their prices have gone up too, and some of the cheapest models have stopped being made at all. When the phone you bought because it was cheap isn't cheap anymore, an iPhone stops looking so far away.Wanting one, and affording oneFor people who aspire to own Apple's newest hardware, and it has become a strong aspiration again, the question is turning into how to keep an iPhone within reach at all. You hold on to one longer. You trade it in. You buy refurbished, you wait for the sales or you stretch the payments out. None of it makes the phone any cheaper.And none of it can be fixed at this end either. Building phones in India closed the distance between the American price and ours, and it did that job well for five years. But a phone assembled here is still full of imported parts bought in dollars, so when the cost moved from the shipping container to the inside of the device, the advantage this market spent a decade building simply didn't apply.Apple can still earn more from India while selling fewer phones, but that is a different growth story from bringing more Indians into its ecosystem. The festive season will show how much room is left between wanting an iPhone and being able to afford one. Discounts and instalments can soften the price of admission. They can't disguise how much higher the entry fee has been set.Get the latest technology news and updates. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: The iPhone Duo’s hardware doesn’t look special, but its software might be
articles.summary: ﻿Android foldables have done most of this before, but rarely looked so good doing it.
articles.body: With the iPhone Duo, Apple has pulled off a familiar trick. It arrives into a mature Android foldable market with a handful of hardware features we’ve mostly already seen elsewhere, but paired with a level of software polish that makes a lot of them feel new again. It’s those software flourishes that have me excited to try the iPhone Duo when it launches next month, but I’m less convinced that its hardware will be anything special. If Apple had gotten there first, the Duo’s biggest surprise would have been its squat, wide, passport-inspired shape. But its slow-moving supply chain meant that Huawei, Samsung, and Xiaomi all managed to beat Apple to market with similarly sized rivals, so the unusual design already feels fairly familiar — helped by Samsung’s aggressive efforts to market its new design. More has been made of Apple’s efforts to eliminate the foldable display’s crease, which seem to have been largely successful. Apple attributes it to a 100-component hinge, custom adhesives that allow the display layers to “glide” over one another, and a matte finish that reduces glare and reflections to make the crease harder to spot. Trying the phone at Apple’s event yesterday, Verge editor-in-chief Nilay Patel said that you can’t really see the crease, but that “if you go looking for it, you can definitely feel one.” [Media: It sounds, and looks, impressive, but Apple is far from the first to do it. Samsung made great strides in eliminating the crease on its Z Fold 8 and Z Fold 8 Ultra thanks to new titanium display layers. Before that, Oppo all but eliminated its Find N6 crease by using 3D printing to fill the minute gaps across the hinge. I’d have to see all those phones side by side to see which crease is subtlest, but even if Apple does win, it won’t be by much. None of the iPhone Duo’s other standout hardware features are true firsts either. Google beat it to an IP68 rating, now even surpassed by Honor’s IP69. Samsung, Oppo, and Honor have all offered stylus support before — though Samsung has since dropped it. Samsung also moved on from the under-display selfie camera, which has always been hamstrung by poor photo and video quality and a distractingly visible patch on the screen. [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: In other ways, the hardware even feels behind the competition. The Duo is the thickest of this new wave of wide foldables, though at 5.2mm when open it’s still thinner than the iPhone Air. The weight is a more obvious issue: The 254g Duo is 26 percent heavier than the Z Fold 8 — a 53g difference — which is going to be pretty noticeable. You have to go back to 2022’s Z Fold 4 to find a Samsung foldable that’s heavier, TriFold excluded. There’s also no evidence that Apple has adopted silicon-carbon batteries yet, which have allowed Samsung, Motorola, and other Android manufacturers to fit bigger capacities into the smaller spaces of foldable phones. Apple says the phone should still deliver a full 24 hours of regular use, but Honor’s Magic V6 uses silicon-carbon to deliver two days of life. The rear cameras are pretty basic too, with a pair of 48-megapixel shooters and no telephoto. That’s almost an exact match for the cameras on the Z Fold 8, but Google, Motorola, Xiaomi and others are now providing capable triple cameras across their foldable lines, and the iPhone Duo already lags behind. None of this is to say that the Duo looks like a bad piece of hardware. Every foldable phone is a compromise, and Apple has picked a similar set of compromises to Samsung in order to get this phone out the door at $1,999. It looks as good as any Android foldable on paper, but it doesn’t look better than many of them. Where that might change is the software. Google has made an effort to make Android more flexible and adaptable to suit folding phones, while OEMs deliver custom solutions to push things further, but none have rewritten the rulebook quite like Apple. The version of iOS 27 running on the iPhone Duo isn’t the same as on other iPhones, but it doesn’t match the iPad either. The biggest change takes the dock from the bottom of the display and lays it out vertically along the right-hand side. The Dynamic Island is turned vertical and thrown in here too, while the status bar collapses into a small circular icon in the top-right corner. This big change is bolstered by clever little touches throughout, like a dynamic blur effect that shifts as you open the screen, creating a fluidity no Android foldable has so far matched. It’s a total transformation of the iOS layout that specifically has foldables in mind. [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: The point of all that change is to ensure consistency between the outer and inner screens. Open the iPhone Duo on the homescreen and almost everything will stay in place, making the move between screens feel seamless. That effect won’t hold in full-screen apps of course, which will adapt to fill the space, but that right-hand UI rail will be fixed. Locking the whole phone interface to the right-hand edge doesn’t sound great for left-handed users though, who are likely to find the Duo unusually awkward to use unless Apple adds the option to flip everything to the other side. StandBy mode has also been retooled for the Duo. Prop the phone down half-open and it will enter StandBy, letting you use it as a digital photo frame, smart display, or just get quick access to a few key widgets, like the clock. Finally, the $2,000 alarm clock you’ve always dreamed of. [Image: Not everything is as ambitious. Multitasking looks limited so far, with the option to run two apps in split-screen, including two windows of the same app, and save pairs to reopen together. Android rivals offer similar, but support three split-screen apps at once, and often more sitting in flexible, resizeable floating windows. But Apple’s software power doesn’t only lie in its OS. It’s the only phone manufacturer with the influence to shift the app ecosystem at large, and with the Duo it hopes to push third-party developers to adopt its best foldable features. It already showed off Netflix, Slack, and Zoom apps with custom Duo support, in some cases adapting dynamically depending on how flexed the hinge is. [Image: Android foldable features are still rare, with most apps simply changing size to fit the varying screens. Even that has its limits — I found a few apps ran awkwardly on the Fold 8’s short outer display. Apple is likely to have an easier time ensuring developers optimize their apps to suit both of the Duo’s displays. Most apps do little else to take advantage of dual displays, multiple cameras, or semi-open states like a tented mode. A few video apps adapt their playback controls when foldables are half-open, but that’s about it so far. Of course, some of those app developers might take their iOS foldable features and eventually roll them out to Android too, so Apple’s advantage might not last forever. It’ll take more time with the Duo to see exactly how it stacks up against the latest models from the Android side of life. So far it doesn’t look like Apple has surpassed its rivals on the hardware side, but its total control of software may give it an edge regardless.

articles.title: Trump faces blowback with $5,000 dividend promise
articles.summary: President Trump’s pledge to distribute $5,000 to every U.S. adult if Republicans win the midterms is drawing backlash from Republicans and Democrats as the president’s allies are forced to explain and defend the proposition. Fiscal hawks, including Rep. Chip Roy (R-Texas), openly questioned how the government would be able to afford to pay 270 million…
articles.body:
President Trump’s pledge to distribute $5,000 to every U.S. adult if Republicans win the midterms is drawing backlash from Republicans and Democrats as the president’s allies are forced to explain and defend the proposition.

Fiscal hawks, including Rep. Chip Roy (R-Texas), openly questioned how the government would be able to afford to pay 270 million Americans that much money, while others have likened Trump’s proposal to bribery.

“Maybe some of us think dependency is evil & soul-sucking in all its forms,” Roy wrote in a post on the social platform X, referring to Trump’s idea.

Former Rep. Bob Good (R-Va.), who chaired the House Freedom Caucus, referred to Trump’s dividend as a “socialist vote-buying scheme.”

It’s unclear how the president would be able to implement such a move given there are 270 million American adults, meaning the endeavor would cost the government roughly $1.35 trillion.

The president’s latest proposal is not the first time he’s offered dividends to Americans. Trump has repeatedly floated a $2,000 tariff dividend check, as well as a $5,000 Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) dividend. Neither idea has come to fruition.

“$5,000 for the peasants will be in the mail after the election only if you vote Republican, along with those DOGE and tariff money checks,” former Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene (R-Ga.), a staunch Trump critic, wrote in a post on X.

Marc Short, Trump’s former legislative director during his first administration, said Trump’s pledge furthers his second administration’s departure from “fiscal responsibility and conservative economics.”

“The president is a performer and having the pageantry of the convention, he’s going to throw out something,” said Short, who is the board chair of former Vice President Mike Pence’s think tank, Advancing American Freedom.

When pressed on the matter on Fox News, Vice President Vance sought to defend the policy as “a dividend for American workers” that would be funded by tariff revenue.

“We’re taking in an extraordinary amount of revenue because the president of the United States is actually standing up to both foreign companies but also foreign countries who have been taking advantage of America’s workers for pretty much my entire life,” Vance said.

“I don’t think it’s a controversial idea. It’s actually the president of the United States saying we’re all working together. We’re all on the same team, and if we continue to create wealth, that wealth is going to go back to the American people,” he continued.

Short responded to Vance’s comments, arguing it’s “a redistribution of that wealth.”

“You’re not going to outbid Democrat socialists in the midterm election,” he said. “It’s one more step down the populist lane of what can we promise the American people to win their vote.”

But not everyone has been opposed to Trump’s idea.

Sen. Bernie Moreno (R-Ohio) said he will prepare legislation so that the “Trump Dividend” is passed “immediately after” the midterms.

“Every American adult gets $5,000 if the Republicans hold Congress, per President Trump. So basically the Republicans are literally giving you cash, and the Democrats want to take everything away from you. Choice couldn’t be clearer,” said Matthew Boyle, the Washington bureau chief for the conservative outlet Breitbart News.

Meanwhile, former Democratic presidential candidate Andrew Yang, who proposed giving every U.S. adult $1,000 per month, said in a post on X that he has “always liked dividends to the American people.”

One national Republican operative told The Hill that Trump’s dividend announcement was “surprising” but argued it is subject to a double standard.

“The whole concept of government handouts continues to get a ton of much-warranted criticism from the right, but it’s interesting to see the level of scrutiny for this plan and not equal scrutiny for the endless handouts from the left,” the operative said. “The president’s idea is that he wants more money into the pockets of the American people and into the U.S. economy while the Democrats would rather fund their socialist wish-list that would only hurt American workers.”

articles.body: Jeremy Clarkson has revealed that he is now in remission from prostate cancer after undergoing treatment for the aggressive disease. The television presenter, best known for Top Gear, The Grand Tour and Clarkson’s Farm, discussed his health in an interview with The Times, explaining that his cancer was detected following a routine blood test and a positive result from the Stockholm3 test, a prostate cancer screening test that combines blood markers, genetic information and medical history.Clarkson's diagnosis was also featured prominently in the latest season of his Prime Video farming series, where viewers saw him navigate the uncertainty surrounding his health and eventually undergo treatment.Despite the seriousness of the diagnosis, Clarkson has maintained his trademark blunt and irreverent approach to discussing his health.Jeremy Clarkson on changing his lifestyleFollowing his diagnosis, Clarkson was advised to make changes to his diet and lifestyle, including eating less fat, consuming more protein and reducing his alcohol intake.However, the broadcaster made it clear that he does not intend to completely abandon the food and drink he enjoys.“Sure, I can eat less and more healthily. I can become a herbivore. And yes, I can go for 20-mile hikes and do 20,000 steps a day,” Clarkson told The Times.“But the truth is, there has to be some joy in life as well.”He added that giving up alcohol and foods such as pork chops would take away some of the pleasure he wants to have in later life.“And I haven’t worked my arse off for 40 years to have no joy in my old age. So, I’m having joy in my old age,” he said.Clarkson's comments reflect his characteristically outspoken attitude, although his remarks do not mean that lifestyle changes are irrelevant after a cancer diagnosis. Medical advice is individual, and patients are generally encouraged to discuss diet, alcohol consumption and exercise with their healthcare teams.Jeremy Clarkson underwent HIFU treatment for prostate cancerClarkson said he underwent high-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU) as part of his treatment.HIFU is a minimally invasive treatment that uses high-frequency sound waves to heat and destroy targeted tissue. Clarkson said he was unwell for a short period following the procedure but has since been doing considerably better.Describing how his cancer was detected, he explained that he undergoes regular health checks.“I get checked every year. And suddenly, oops, there’s a little thing here,” he said.According to Clarkson, doctors then presented him with a range of treatment options.The presenter also acknowledged some of the more difficult moments surrounding his diagnosis, including having to tell his children that he had cancer and undergoing catheterisation.“Basically, it is choosing what sort of thing you want in your bottom,” Clarkson said in his typically candid style. “Yes, it is not very nice having to tell your children, ‘I’ve got cancer’, neither is having a catheter fitted. But otherwise, no problem.”Jeremy Clarkson jokes about living for another six yearsEven while discussing cancer and mortality, Clarkson has continued to inject humour into conversations about his future.In the same interview, he joked that he had made financial plans that involved living for at least another six years.“I have a tax plan. I have made arrangements. To live for at least seven more years... Actually, six more years now. And then, if I accidentally croak, I'll be happy,” he said.The remark was made in the context of inheritance tax and gifting rules, rather than as a literal prediction about his life expectancy.Clarkson has faced other health concerns in recent years. In 2024, he revealed that he had experienced a serious heart problem, before his prostate cancer diagnosis was subsequently discussed on Clarkson’s Farm.Jeremy Clarkson’s prostate cancer diagnosis raises awarenessClarkson's decision to discuss his prostate cancer publicly has also had an impact beyond television.Prostate Cancer UK reported an increase in visitors to its website following his announcement, with the charity saying his openness helped encourage more people to seek information about prostate cancer.The development comes amid growing attention around prostate cancer screening and early detection in the UK.The Stockholm3 test, which Clarkson underwent, combines several indicators to assess the risk of clinically significant prostate cancer. A new initiative is reportedly set to make the test available to thousands of men aged 45 to 74 at a substantially reduced cost, while some men on lower incomes will be able to access it free through the NHS.The wider conversation has also been amplified by Olympic cycling champion Sir Chris Hoy, who has spoken publicly about his own experience with terminal prostate cancer and the importance of cancer awareness and early detection.Clarkson’s Farm wins at National Television AwardsClarkson's health update comes shortly after a major professional milestone.On Tuesday, September 8, Clarkson’s Farm won the Reality Docuseries award at the National Television Awards, recognising the popularity of the Prime Video series.The show follows Clarkson's attempts to operate his Diddly Squat Farm in Oxfordshire, chronicling the challenges of farming, bureaucracy, weather and business alongside regular appearances from Kaleb Cooper, Lisa Hogan and Gerald Cooper.The success of Clarkson’s Farm has helped introduce the outspoken broadcaster to a new generation of viewers, while also giving audiences a much more personal look at his life away from motoring television.Get the latest TV News, TV Shows and more. articles.title: Electric air taxis get the green light for test flights in Texas
articles.summary: Electric and autonomous aircraft will take flight over Texas as part of a weeklong demonstration for the federal government’s new pilot program.
articles.body: A new federal program to test the feasibility of electric, hybrid-electric, and autonomous aircraft kicks off today in Texas — before the rules governing this new technology have even been finalized. Earlier this year, the Federal Aviation Administration’s Advanced Air Mobility and Electric Vertical Takeoff and Landing (eVTOL) Integration Pilot Program (eIPP) selected eight state-led projects to serve as some of the first public tests of these new aircraft. The first one kicks off today in Texas, featuring three eVTOL companies: Joby, Beta, and Wisk. For the next week, these companies will conduct test flights demonstrating future routes between cities and regional airports, including Dallas Fort Worth International Airport. The aircraft won’t carry any passengers, but regulators will be keen to see how the state’s air traffic control system handles the uptick in flight traffic. The companies, meanwhile, are eager to prove to the federal government that their aircraft deserve to be awarded type certification, which is required before any of them can carry passengers commercially in the US. [Media: But type certification can take years to attain, which led to the White House to create this pilot program allowing these companies to demonstrate their new technology — even before the regulatory process has concluded. Through the eIPP, the companies hope to accelerate their path to market by getting a head start on data collection that will be needed for certification. Data from the program will also be used to “develop new regulations that safely enable this futuristic technology at scale,” the White House said earlier. The companies say they are thrilled to demonstrate the future of electric and autonomous flight, which they argue will help reduce car traffic in cities and open up new mobility opportunities for consumers. “I’m incredibly excited by the potential for vertical lift in Texas, a state with the infrastructure, expertise, and partnerships to help lead the next era of American aviation,” JoeBen Bevirt, Founder and CEO of Joby Aviation, said in a statement. Several of these companies have conducted public test flights before — Joby’s egg-shaped aircraft demonstrated its future route between Lower Manhattan and JFK Airprot earlier this year — but these will be the first official flights under the White House’s new pilot program. Additional tests are being planned in New York, Utah, Pennsylvania, Louisiana, Florida, North Carolina, and New Mexico. Legal in-fighting, however, could muddy the picture for electric aviation. Joby and one of its rivals, Archer, are currently suing each other for stolen trade secrets and corporate espionage. Technology limitations, including battery weight and sensor decisions, could also hamper the rollout.

articles.title: 5 things to know about Trump’s $5K dividend pledge
articles.summary: President Trump pledged Wednesday to dole out $5,000 dividends to U.S. adults only if Republicans keep their control of Congress after the fall midterm elections, the latest financial promise he has made across his two presidencies. The president announced the proposed “Trump dividends” while speaking at the Republican National Committee’s (RNC) midterm convention in Dallas.…
articles.body:
President Trump pledged Wednesday to dole out $5,000 dividends to U.S. adults only if Republicans keep their control of Congress after the fall midterm elections, the latest financial promise he has made across his two presidencies.

The president announced the proposed “Trump dividends” while speaking at the Republican National Committee’s (RNC) midterm convention in Dallas. He said his administration can disburse these dividends to the country’s roughly 270 million adults “because we’ve done so well and because our country is making so much money.”

Few other details were initially released about the payments, similar to other pledges he has made to pay Americans that were vague on specific details.

Here are five things to know about Trump’s $5,000 promise:

Dividends would cost $1.2 trillion in total, though Trump did not specify how it would be funded. The amount compares to the $1.27 trillion spent on interest on the national debt, as well as the $1.36 trillion committed to this year’s defense spending.

It is not yet clear if Congress would have to approve the dividend. Last year, Trump gave U.S. service members $1,776 checks that were drawn from funds appropriated by Congress.

Lawmakers approved and Trump signed off on two rounds of $1,200 stimulus checks for Americans during the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020, using $2.2 trillion allocated by the Coronavirus Aid, Relief, and Economic Security (CARES) Act.

This latest pledge follows several others during Trump’s second term that have not materialized.

Trump has proposed , since last year, checks of up to $2,000 from revenue generated by his administration’s tariffs. He suggested that the revenue generated by the import tax on foreign goods would pay down the country’s debt and put money in the pockets of “everyone” except “high-income people.”

Those checks have not become reality since the Supreme Court struck down the bulk of the president’s sweeping tariffs earlier this year.

Tesla CEO Elon Musk proposed $5,000 dividend checks early in Trump’s second term while operating the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE). Trump backed Musk’s idea, which aimed to use the estimated $2 trillion DOGE sought to cut from federal spending to make up the dividends.

The Trump administration is also promising $500 rebate checks to around 1 million Affordable Care Act enrollees in 30 states. The White House claimed that the Biden administration “accumulated a significant surplus of funds that were not used” to help Americans paying high premiums.

Trump also proposed a 10-percent middle-class tax cut in October 2018, just before that year’s midterms. He said he would push for it after the midterms, but he repeated his pledge with his eye toward GOP control of Congress after the 2020 elections.

The pledge comes as Trump faces increasing pressure over the state of the economy, which could be the deciding factor in who controls Congress next year.

Polling has regularly shown that Americans are concerned about the high cost of living and affordability, though Trump has brushed these concerns aside, previously calling affordability a hoax perpetrated by Democrats.

Rising energy costs have also been driven by the Iran war, which has been consistently unpopular for more than six months. Trump has also dismissed concerns about high gas prices, suggesting that gas prices will “ drop precipitously ” after the conflict ends, which he does not expect will happen before the midterms.

The cost of some goods is also set to rise after Canada’s 50 percent retaliatory tariffs took effect earlier this week amid Trump’s trade war with the U.S.’s northern neighbor. The escalating trade war could pose a challenge to Republican candidates in battleground states that border Canada.

Marc Goldwein, senior policy director at the Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget, warned that the dividends could add to inflation, which dropped slightly in July to 3.4 percent .

“I have to pull out our old inflation model, but I think it’s likely something like this would create an extra 1.5 points of inflationary pressure (some which would be canceled with higher interest rate rates) and boost output by a quarter point or so,” Goldwein wrote Wednesday on the social platform X .

He wrote in a separate post that the dividends would also result in “a huge spike in the deficit.” Goldwein pointed to the economic impact of the COVID-19-era stimulus checks under the first Trump administration and the Biden administration, which some experts have argued may have greatly contributed to soaring inflation in the years after the pandemic.

The U.S. national debt crossed $40 trillion last month.

Congress will likely need to step in to make Trump’s pledge a reality. One GOP senator has said he will introduce such legislation.

“I will get a bill ready so that we can get the Trump Dividend passed immediately after the November 3rd election … because Republicans (and America) will win!” Sen. Bernie Moreno (R-Ohio) wrote Wednesday night on X .

But not all Republican lawmakers favored Trump’s pledge, with Rep. Chip Roy (R-Texas) writing on X that “dependency is evil & soul-sucking in all its forms.”

Trump’s past pledges to give checks to Americans have not materialized without legislation to accompany them and congressional approval. Stimulus checks for individual Americans and small businesses that were distributed during the COVID-19 pandemic won the support of Congress as part of the CARES Act.

National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett has suggested that Congress would have to sign off on Trump’s tariff checks.
